chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: Ellington versus Strayhorn
summary: They compare Strayhorn's trained, nearly white style with Ellington's self-acquired music, and agree Ellington was untouchable and produced more after Strayhorn died.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: -- some of the -- like, when Strayhorn came in, now, when I came -- moved here in '59, there was some of them wanted to tell me that Strayhorn had written far more
important things than Duke, and that Duke's reputation had been very much built up by Strayhorn. But --
No, I know the difference now. I can hear difference. It's the same as night and day on Duke --
A lot of people want to ______ you can't tell the difference, but you can.
Strayhorn, (inaudible), Strayhorn is pretty close to a white writer, white music, you know what I mean?
He had legitimate training.
Sure, (inaudible) make it like that.
And Duke's thing was all -- I mean, most of it was self-acquired, wasn't it, came out of his head.
Come out of the man's head instead of the book.
No, I think the things -- I mean, Billy did write some great things.
Wonderful things.
Especially some of those things he did for Johnny Hodges, you know, those ballad type (inaudible).
Yes.
But, you know, I mean, people sort of forget that it was Duke who wrote (inaudible), which was just as good as any of those ballad things that ______ wrote.
I'll tell you another thing. When you
reach out and get a man like Strayhorn, Duke's going to get a little lazy --
That's right.
-- in making do, and he's going to ease up on his --
That's right.
But now I realize Duke -- boy, that stuff is untouchable. Some of the things that he really did.

What proves that is that after Strayhorn died, he wrote -- really, he turned out more music after Strayhorn died than he did at any other period. No, I quite agree, I think. Strayhorn was like a crutch that he didn't need, really.
Yeah.
